hooks.text: A 1,100-mile cloud appears over a Martian volcano every morning.
Why does a 1,100-mile cloud form over Mars every morning?
Clouds on Mars freeze straight out of thin air without dust.

title: The Martian Volcano That Freezes Air Without Dust
description: Every morning on Mars, a 1,100-mile water-ice cloud forms over the giant volcano Arsia Mons. Scientists discovered it freezes spontaneously out of thin air without any dust particles.

beats.text: A 1,100-mile cloud appears over a Martian volcano every morning.
beats.visual: Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud imaged by Mars Express Visual Monitoring Camera
queries: Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud Mars Express

beats.text: It races westward at 380 miles per hour, then vanishes before noon.
beats.visual: Mars Express HRSC image of Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud expanding westward

beats.text: The cloud grows high above Arsia Mons, a volcano 12 miles tall.
beats.visual: THEMIS infrared mosaic of the giant Martian volcano Arsia Mons

beats.text: ESA tracked this daily lifecycle using an ordinary webcam on Mars Express.
beats.visual: Artist concept of ESA Mars Express orbiter in orbit around Mars

beats.text: Earth clouds need dust or pollen particles to freeze around.
beats.visual: Diagram illustrating cloud microphysics and heterogeneous nucleation around dust particles

beats.text: But Arsia Mons forces air upward, dropping temperatures 54 degrees in ten minutes.
beats.visual: Topographical map showing steep slopes of Arsia Mons in Tharsis region

beats.text: Water vapor freezes spontaneously straight out of clean air.
beats.visual: Diagram showing homogeneous ice nucleation without pre-existing seed particles

beats.text: This impossible morning frost builds a giant feature across the planet.
beats.visual: Viking 2 orbiter photograph of Mars showing early morning clouds
